speaker: Unknown
en: I joined Lumentum at a time where board of directors showed me a forecast and they said, hey, here's what we think the company is going to do.
zh: 我加入 Lumentum 的时候,董事会给我看了一份预测,他们说,嘿,这是我们认为公司将要做的业绩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I, of course, discounted it by about 50%.
zh: 当然,我把它打了大约 50% 的折扣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been probably 4x over what they even showed me.
zh: 而实际结果大概是他们给我看的数字的 4 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been there about five quarters now.
zh: 我在那里待了大约五个季度了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in those five quarters, we've tripled our top line revenue.
zh: 在这五个季度里,我们的营收翻了三倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the stock price has gone up 10 or 12 times.
zh: 所以股价上涨了 10 到 12 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point, it was up over $1,000.
zh: 曾一度涨到超过 1000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a high-performing stock largely because people are seeing the future.
zh: 我们的股票表现出色,很大程度上是因为人们看到了未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we're being asked by these hyperscalers to deploy in millions, tens of millions in units.
zh: 现在这些超大规模云厂商要求我们以数百万、数千万的量级去部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really changed the dynamic in our industry.
zh: 所以这真的改变了我们行业的格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just for Lumentum, every single optical company now is dealing with different scales than we ever had before.
zh: 不仅仅是 Lumentum,现在每一家光通信公司都在应对我们以前从未有过的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question we get all the time, and I think you've asked many of the people on your show, is, is this a bubble?
zh: 我们经常被问到的一个问题——我想你也问过你节目上的很多嘉宾——就是,这是泡沫吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Michael, welcome to Sorcery.
zh: Michael,欢迎来到 Sorcery。

speaker: Unknown
en: Molly, thanks for having me on.
zh: Molly,感谢你邀请我来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really a pleasure.
zh: 真的很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're here in Paris at Ray's.
zh: 我们现在在巴黎的 Ray's。

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you just on stage?
zh: 你刚才在台上吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What were you doing over there?
zh: 你在那边做什么了?

speaker: Unknown
en: I was on stage.
zh: 我在台上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I gave a keynote with Tony Kim, and I think Tony Kim was over here earlier today talking to you, so you got all the celebs, I guess.
zh: 我和 Tony Kim 做了一场主题演讲,我记得 Tony Kim 今天早些时候也在这里和你聊过,所以你把所有名人都请到了,我想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's a big fan of you, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句,他是你的铁杆粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't know if you knew that.
zh: 我不知道你是否知道这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's a big fan of yours, too.
zh: 他也是你的铁杆粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: He told me, he goes, this is a great setup.
zh: 他告诉我,他说,这个访谈 setups 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll enjoy it.
zh: 你会喜欢的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, a lot of fun talking to Molly.
zh: 我就想,和 Molly 聊天会很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there we go.
zh: 那就这样吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what did you guys talk about on stage?
zh: 那你们在台上聊了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Optics is becoming a big thing, right, in the data centers.
zh: 光学正在成为数据中心的一件大事,对吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Tony was sort of framing.
zh: Tony 大致在做框架性介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have all these funny terms, scale across, scale out, scale up, scale in.
zh: 我们有各种有趣的术语,scale across、scale out、scale up、scale in。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Tony was walking the audience through what all of these different things mean.
zh: Tony 带着观众逐一讲解这些不同的概念分别是什么意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: What Lumentum's role is in all of that, which is we're in the middle of a pretty exciting time right now as the data center uses more and more optical connectivity.
zh: Lumentum 在其中扮演的角色是什么——我们现在正处于一个非常激动人心的时期,因为数据中心越来越多地使用光连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for people who don't know what optical connectivity means, can you explain that?
zh: 那么对于不了解光连接含义的人,你能解释一下吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We're moving from copper wires to optics and transferring data with light, but what does that mean?
zh: 我们正在从铜线转向光学,用光来传输数据,但这意味着什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously there are fibers and fibers are essentially glass.
zh: 显然有光纤,光纤本质上就是玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just conductors.
zh: 它们只是导体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of having wires, copper wires, you have fibers and fibers basically contains the light just like a wire or a copper strand contains electricity.
zh: 不是用导线、铜线,而是用光纤,光纤基本上把光约束在里面,就像导线或铜线把电约束在里面一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what you get with fiber optics is the ability to move data faster over longer distances with less heat and less power than you get with electricity.
zh: 所以光纤给你带来的能力是,与用电传输相比,能够以更少的热量和更少的功耗在更长的距离上更快地传输数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about the way data centers are architected today, it's mostly copper wires, right?
zh: 所以如果你想想当今数据中心的架构方式,大部分都是铜线,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Ethernet cables are essentially copper wires.
zh: 以太网线本质上就是铜线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And copper wires, the physics of copper is there's a resistive property.
zh: 而铜线的物理特性是有电阻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as data tries to move across the wires, it gets hotter and the resistance prevents it from going all that far.
zh: 所以当数据试图通过铜线传输时,它会发热,而电阻使其无法传输太远的距离。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now inside the data center, you have speeds are increasing, bandwidths are increasing, and copper can no longer carry these signals the distances they need to go.
zh: 所以现在在数据中心内部,速度在提升,带宽在提升,铜线已经无法把这些信号传输到需要的距离了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have more and more optics now coming into the data center.
zh: 所以现在有越来越多的光学进入数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And optics essentially is just light, right?
zh: 而光学本质上就是光,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just shining light along a fiber.
zh: 我们只是让光沿着一根光纤传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that light is modulated, meaning it turns on and off at really, really high speeds.
zh: 那光是被调制的,意思是它以非常非常高的速度开和关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what creates the transmission.
zh: 这就是产生传输的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was Tony, we were on a call before our interview and he was pointing out the great irony of spending $10 trillion over the next couple of years on data center build out to move data from meters down to centimeters and millimeters.
zh: 我记得是 Tony,我们在访谈前通了一次电话,他指出了一个巨大的讽刺:未来几年花 10 万亿美元建设数据中心,却是为了让数据从几米的距离缩短到几厘米、几毫米。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how is this process and this build out?
zh: 那么这个过程和这轮建设是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you managing it?
zh: 你们是怎么管理的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, look, I mean, you know, fiber optics has been the backbone of the internet for years, right?
zh: 是这样,你知道,光纤多年来一直是互联网的骨干,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So when the internet first came in was the sort of the first great wave of the optical companies.
zh: 所以互联网刚出现时,是光学公司的第一波大浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what happened was you're digging up the earth.
zh: 当时的情况是,你在挖掘土地,

speaker: Unknown
en: in the United States, in Paris, in London, wherever it might be, and installing these fiber optic cables because the internet now is traveling over huge distances.
zh: 在美国、在巴黎、在伦敦,无论哪里,铺设这些光纤电缆,因为互联网当时要跨越很远的距离传输。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the first real optical sort of the big wave was now building the backbone of our internet infrastructure across the world.
zh: 所以第一波真正的光学浪潮,就是在全世界范围内建设我们互联网基础设施的骨干。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you actually have fiber optic cables today that run under the ocean.
zh: 而且今天确实有光纤电缆铺设在海底。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we want to have communication that goes between Paris and New York, there are fiber optic cables that are actually buried in the ocean and those fiber optic cables conduct these signals.
zh: 所以如果我们想要巴黎和纽约之间的通信,就有光纤电缆真正埋在海洋里,这些光纤电缆传导这些信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as I said a minute ago, what's happened is now you're going to faster and faster speeds.
zh: 但正如我刚才所说,现在的速度越来越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you go to faster and faster speeds, the physics say that copper can't work or it doesn't work as well.
zh: 当速度越来越快时,物理规律表明铜线就行不通了,或者说效果不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what you have now is this internet, this big backbone, this big infrastructure that we've played in for numerous decades.
zh: 所以现在你面对的是这个互联网、这个大骨干、这个我们已经参与了几十年的大基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those volumes are actually relatively modest.
zh: 而且那些产量其实相对温和。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're talking about volumes of, let's say, 1,000 units a quarter.
zh: 你说的是,比方说,每季度 1,000 个单位的产量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we're being asked by these hyperscalers to deploy in millions, tens of millions of units.
zh: 而现在这些超大规模云厂商要求我们部署数百万、数千万个单位。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really changed the dynamic in our industry, not just for Lumentum, but I think every single optical company now is dealing with different scales than we ever had before.
zh: 所以这真的改变了我们行业的格局,不仅是 Lumentum,我认为现在每一家光学公司都在应对我们以前从未经历过的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it like, and I'm sure there's lots of challenges, but what is it actually tangibly like getting spun up in these new data centers?
zh: 是什么样的,我知道肯定有很多挑战,但在这些新数据中心里真正启动起来,具体是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What actually goes on behind the scenes?
zh: 幕后到底发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of manufacturing.
zh: 有大量的制造工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think if you, you know, you obviously know the industry super well.
zh: 我是说,你知道,你显然对这个行业非常了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you talk to companies like NVIDIA, Broadcom, they manufacture most of their products at TSMC.
zh: 我是说,你和像 NVIDIA、Broadcom 这样的公司谈过,他们大部分产品都在 TSMC 制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they essentially outsource the manufacturing problem.
zh: 所以他们基本上把制造问题外包了出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: The optics industry doesn't have that luxury, right?
zh: 而光学行业没有这种奢侈条件,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very sort of niche industry.
zh: 这是一个非常小众的行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one that's grown up over multiple decades.
zh: 它是历经几十年发展起来的行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us, we actually operate our own fabs.
zh: 所以对我们来说,我们实际上运营着自己的晶圆厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in some respect, we're like the TSMC of the optical industry.
zh: 从某种角度看,我们就像是光学行业里的 TSMC。

speaker: Unknown
en: Optics depends on a different material.
zh: 光学依赖一种不同的材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: Semiconductors use something called CMOS, and all of the semiconductors that you know well are built on CMOS, memories built on CMOS.
zh: 半导体使用一种叫 CMOS 的东西,你所熟知的所有半导体都建立在 CMOS 上,存储器建立在 CMOS 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: TPUs are built on CMOS.
zh: TPU 建立在 CMOS 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: The NVIDIA GPU is built on CMOS.
zh: NVIDIA GPU 建立在 CMOS 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: But lasers and fiber optics are built on a different material called indium phosphide.
zh: 但激光器和光纤建立在一种不同的材料上,叫做磷化铟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of a mouthful, but it's this indium phosphide.
zh: 有点拗口,但就是这种磷化铟。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a very boutique thing.
zh: 而这是一种非常小众的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little more of a niche.
zh: 它更加冷门一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we actually have to make our own indium phosphide products.
zh: 所以我们实际上必须自己制造磷化铟产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to manufacture those ourselves.
zh: 我们必须自己生产那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that requires pretty long lead times, right?
zh: 而这需要相当长的前置时间,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes us multiple years to build a fab.
zh: 建一座晶圆厂需要我们好几年时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it requires a lot of expense.
zh: 而且需要大量开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're a very CapEx heavy company.
zh: 所以我们是一家资本支出非常重的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spend a lot in trying to build out and manufacture our products.
zh: 我们花很多钱去扩建和制造我们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it takes a while.
zh: 而且这需要时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a bottleneck that's developing.
zh: 所以正在形成一个瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you talked about it with Tony.
zh: 我记得你和 Tony 谈到过这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as these fiber optics becomes more and more prevalent in data center, it's creating an ever tighter noose around the industry because there's only so much we can do so quickly.
zh: 随着光纤在数据中心越来越普及,它正在给这个行业套上一个越来越紧的绞索,因为我们能快速做的事情毕竟有限。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Brex, my favorite.
zh: 本期节目由 Brex 为您带来,我的最爱。

speaker: Unknown
en: You become what you spend on, and I refuse to spend my time on work that shouldn't exist.
zh: 你花钱花在什么上面,你就会成为什么,而我拒绝把时间花在不该存在的工作上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Expense reports, receipt chasing, and manual closes.
zh: 报销单、追讨收据和手工结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies building what's next from Vercel, OpenAI, Anthropic, Granola, and Deepgram all made the same call.
zh: 那些正在构建未来的公司——Vercel、OpenAI、Anthropic、Granola 和 Deepgram——都做出了同样的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all run on Brex.
zh: 它们都运行在 Brex 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brex is the intelligent finance platform that combines cards, expenses, and banking into a single stack.
zh: Brex 是智能金融平台,将卡片、费用和银行业务整合到一个栈中。

speaker: Unknown
en: With agentic finance built in.
zh: 内置智能体金融。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI agents that handle expenses automatically, enforce policy before spend happens, and close your books in minutes.
zh: AI 智能体自动处理费用、在支出发生前执行政策,并在几分钟内完成账目结算。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why Sorcery runs on Brex, so I can spend time on building and not busy work.
zh: 这就是 Sorcery 运行在 Brex 上的原因,这样我可以把时间花在构建上,而不是琐事上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's time to get Brex AF.
zh: 是时候 get Brex AF 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at Brex.com slash Sorcery.
zh: 了解更多请访问 Brex.com/sorcery。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's B-R-E-X dot com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 也就是 B-R-E-X dot com 斜杠 S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bye.
zh: 再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: That supply constraint is creating a lot of demand, but it's also creating tremendous demand for the stock, which is crazy to see.
zh: 这种供应限制创造了很多需求,但它也为股票创造了巨大的需求,这看起来非常疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: The stock was up, I think, almost a thousand percent at one point.
zh: 股价曾一度上涨,我记得,接近百分之千。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you handle that mentally as a CEO when you know that you are constrained?
zh: 作为 CEO,当你知道自己受到限制时,你在心理上是如何应对的?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's tough.
zh: 这很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the interesting thing, the question we get all the time, and I think you've asked many of the people on your show, is, is this a bubble, right?
zh: 我的意思是,有意思的是,我们经常被问到的一个问题,我想你也问过你节目里的很多人,就是:这是个泡沫吗,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's interesting about the optical industry is if there are no more data center build outs, if you don't see this crazy rate of construction that we've seen over the past three or four years,
zh: 而光学行业有意思的地方在于,即使不再有更多的数据中心建设,即使你看不到过去三四年来我们见过的这种疯狂的建设速度,

speaker: Unknown
en: Still, you're going to have a shift within the existing properties from electrical signaling to optics, right?
zh: 即便如此,在现有设施内部,也会出现从电信号向光学的转变,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our growth rate, which has been astronomical, we've grown three times.
zh: 所以我们的增长率,一直是天文数字,我们增长了三倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been with the company only a short period of time.
zh: 我在公司任职的时间还很短。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been there about five quarters now.
zh: 我在那儿大约五个季度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in those five quarters, we've tripled our top line revenue.
zh: 在这五个季度里,我们的营收翻了三倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the stock price has gone up 10 or 12 times.
zh: 所以股价上涨了十到十二倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you correctly point out, at one point it was up over $1,000.
zh: 正如你正确指出的,曾一度上涨超过 1000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's come back, I think, on a lot of the concern around AI over the last couple of weeks.
zh: 我觉得,过去几周,由于对 AI 的许多担忧,它有所回落。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have a high performing stock largely because people are seeing the future and seeing the future start to play out where you have more and more optical components going into these data centers and driving super high demand for our products.
zh: 但我们的股票表现出色,主要是因为人们看到了未来,看到未来开始展开:越来越多的光学组件进入这些数据中心,并对我们的产品产生极高的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you joined a CEO in 2025.
zh: 所以你在 2025 年以 CEO 身份加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it like to take the reins in the craziest market ever?
zh: 在有史以来最疯狂的市场中接管一家公司是什么感觉?

speaker: Unknown
en: And also give a little bit of your background of where you were before.
zh: 另外也简单介绍一下你之前的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, this is an interesting thing.
zh: 好的,我是说,这是一件很有意思的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you look at most CEOs, they either retire or somebody retires them for them, right?
zh: 我认为如果你看看大多数 CEO,他们要么退休,要么被别人让他们退休,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't see too many CEOs change jobs.
zh: 你不会看到太多 CEO 换工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've actually been lucky enough now to be CEO of three different public companies.
zh: 而我其实很幸运,现在已经是三家不同上市公司的 CEO 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first public company I was a CEO of is a company called Finisar that was optical.
zh: 我担任 CEO 的第一家上市公司是一家叫 Finisar 的公司,是做光学的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's now the heartbeat of one of our biggest competitors, but also one of our biggest partners in Coherent.
zh: 它现在是我们最大竞争对手之一 Coherent 的核心,但同时也是我们最大的合作伙伴之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coherent's built around the engine that was Finisar that we ended up selling to them.
zh: Coherent 是围绕曾经属于 Finisar 的引擎建立的,那个引擎是我们最终卖给他们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I was the CEO of a semiconductor company.
zh: 之后我是一家半导体公司的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm mostly a semiconductor guy, and I was CEO of a company called Synaptics for five or six years.
zh: 我基本上是个半导体人,我在一家叫 Synaptics 的公司做了五六年 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I joined Lumentum, as you're pointing out, at a time where
zh: 然后我加入了 Lumentum,正如你所指出的,在那个时点,

speaker: Unknown
en: The board of directors showed me a forecast and they said, hey, here's what we think the company is going to do.
zh: 董事会给我看了一份预测,他们说,嘿,这是我们认为公司将会做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I, of course, as one does, discounted it by about 50%.
zh: 而我,当然,像常人一样,把它打了大约五折。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been up probably 4X over what they even showed me.
zh: 结果实际表现比他们给我看的还要高出大约四倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've just hit the company with the right products at absolutely the right time, really.
zh: 所以,说真的,我们只是让公司在绝对正确的时机推出了完全正确的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Team, before I got there, the previous CEO set it up well, right products, right roadmap, and we have all of the goods that people are looking for now as they convert their data centers to more and more of the fiber optics.
zh: 还有团队,在我来之前,前任 CEO 打下了很好的基础,正确的产品、正确的路线图,而随着人们把数据中心越来越多地转向光纤,我们现在拥有人们所寻找的所有好东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you manage that plan and keep pivoting the strategy as you overperform?
zh: 你是如何管理这个计划,并在超额完成的情况下不断调整战略的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, what we've tried to do, Molly, is simplify.
zh: 实际上,Molly,我们试图做的是简化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think when I came into the company, there was a lot of products that were geared toward the old telecom industry, selling still to AT&T, to Verizon.
zh: 我认为我刚进入公司时,有很多产品是面向旧电信行业的,仍然卖给 AT&T、Verizon。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were products that we were doing that were around industrial lasers, interestingly enough.
zh: 我们还有一些产品,有意思的是,是围绕工业激光器的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lasers are used to cut metal for car doors.
zh: 激光器被用来切割金属,比如车门。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're used to machine different parts.
zh: 它们被用来加工各种零件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had a business in that.
zh: 我们在那方面有一块业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I've done is said, okay, look, let's focus our efforts on the data center.
zh: 而我所做的是说,好,看,让我们把精力集中在数据中心上。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's enough here going on that we really want to simplify our business as much as we possibly can, focus on where we think the biggest opportunities are, and that's the data center.
zh: 这里有足够多的事情在发生,我们真的想尽可能简化我们的业务,聚焦于我们认为最大的机会在哪里,那就是数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've almost become a pure play data center.
zh: 所以我们几乎变成了一家纯粹的数据中心公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got some risk, right?
zh: 是有风险,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If the data center ends up rolling over and that market hiccups a bit, we'll be caught.
zh: 如果数据中心最终垮掉,那个市场打了个嗝,我们就会被套住。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't think that that's going to happen.
zh: 但我不认为那会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if, as I said a minute ago, you start seeing a slowdown in data center builds, we're in really, really good shape because you still see a conversion inside the data center from electrical to optical.
zh: 而且,就像我刚才说的,即使你开始看到数据中心建设放缓,我们的处境也会非常非常好,因为你仍然会看到数据中心内部从电到光的转换。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, they're going to space.
zh: 另外,他们要上太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're also going to space.
zh: 而且他们也要上太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our buddies at SpaceX are trying to do these build outs.
zh: 我们在 SpaceX 的朋友们正在尝试做这些扩建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, lasers are super important for all the same reasons.
zh: 显然,出于所有同样的原因,激光超级重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can put a laser in the ocean and transmit across the Pacific, you can certainly put lasers in space and create this reality of an internet in space, right?
zh: 如果你能把激光器放进海底并横跨太平洋传输,那你当然可以把激光器放进太空,创造出太空互联网这个现实,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be necessary.
zh: 这将会是必要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a high degree of difficulty outside the lasers, but we can help enable that.
zh: 激光器之外的难度很高,但我们可以帮助实现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also sounds super cool.
zh: 这听起来也超级酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is.
zh: 确实是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is super cool.
zh: 确实超级酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you know, lasers are used today, as you likely know, in things like the Iron Dome, right?
zh: 我是说,你知道,如你可能知道的,激光今天被用于像铁穹这样的东西,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Lasers you use to shoot down enemy missiles.
zh: 激光被用来击落敌方导弹。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they have been deployed in space.
zh: 所以它们已经被部署到太空了。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are not nearly as powerful as those things.
zh: 这些远没有那些东西那么强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we've had a lot of experience as an industry and certainly our company in deploying products in space.
zh: 但作为一个行业,当然还有我们公司,在太空部署产品方面已经有很多经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really good point.
zh: 这是个很好的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, so we did this interview with Tom Mueller, who was the first employee at SpaceX, and we were talking about data centers in space and we put out the videos and the YouTube comments, you know, there's a lot of fear mongering about birds and killing birds with the lasers and all that kind of stuff.
zh: 好,所以我们采访了 Tom Mueller,他是 SpaceX 的第一名员工,我们聊了太空数据中心,我们发布了视频,YouTube 评论里,你知道,有很多关于鸟类的危言耸听,说激光会杀死鸟之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So can you dispel some of the misconceptions about lasers and their strength?
zh: 那么你能澄清一些关于激光及其强度的误解吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And look, it's all about power.
zh: 看,这全关乎功率。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you a really good example, right?
zh: 我给你举一个非常好的例子,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The iPhone with the Face ID, that's a laser product that beams lasers onto your face.
zh: 带有 Face ID 的 iPhone,那是一个激光产品,它把激光束打到你脸上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the concerns, of course, Apple had was, hey, I want to have people's eyes burning out.
zh: 当然,Apple 的一个顾虑是,嘿,我可不想让人们眼睛被烧伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the power of those lasers are relatively modest and you're never going to burn somebody's eye out.
zh: 所以那些激光的功率相对温和,你永远不会再烧坏某人的眼睛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similarly, you're not going to have birds burning up as these lasers shoot data down to the earth.
zh: 同样,当这些激光把数据射向地面时,你也不会有鸟被烧起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It all has to do with the power.
zh: 这一切都与功率有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have these
zh: 你可以拥有这些

speaker: Unknown
en: Super high powered lasers that can shoot down missiles that can cut through metal.
zh: 超高功率的激光器,可以击落导弹,可以切割金属。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have modestly powered lasers that power the internet backbone.
zh: 你可以拥有功率温和的激光器,为互联网骨干网提供动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can have these super low powered lasers that do things like the face ID.
zh: 你也可以拥有这些超低功率的激光器,做像 Face ID 这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty cool.
zh: 这挺酷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're building what's next in AI, you need to know MongoDB.
zh: 如果你在构建 AI 的下一个未来,你需要了解 MongoDB。

speaker: Unknown
en: The database platform developers love and built for the agents you're running.
zh: 这是开发者喜爱的数据库平台,为你正在运行的智能体而构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: MongoDB stores searches and reasons over your data in real time with vector search and embeddings from Voyage AI all in the same system.
zh: MongoDB 通过来自 Voyage AI 的向量搜索和嵌入,在同一个系统中实时存储、搜索并对你的数据进行推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: No separate pipelines, no stitching together 10 different tools.
zh: 不需要单独的管道,不需要把 10 种不同的工具拼接在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's why 75% of the Fortune 100 and leading AI native startups run on MongoDB.
zh: 这就是为什么 75% 的财富 100 强和领先的 AI 原生初创公司在 MongoDB 上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Build and scale from your first user to billions of vectors.
zh: 从你的第一个用户扩展到数十亿个向量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to mongodb.com slash AI to learn more.
zh: 访问 mongodb.com/AI 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's mongodb.com slash AI to learn more.
zh: 那就是 mongodb.com/AI,了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bye.
zh: 再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Assembly AI is a voice AI infrastructure layer millions of developers build on.
zh: Assembly AI 是一个数百万开发者在其上构建的语音 AI 基础设施层。

speaker: Unknown
en: They build the industry's best speech-to-text, voice agent, and speech understanding models that serve as critical infrastructure for companies like Granola, HeyGen, Ashby, and ClickUp.
zh: 他们构建了业界最好的语音转文字、语音智能体和语音理解模型,作为 Granola、HeyGen、Ashby 和 ClickUp 等公司的关键基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their speech-to-text models lead the industry in accuracy and quality, and their speech understanding models help you go beyond transcription by uncovering insights, identifying speakers, and highlighting key information from voice data.
zh: 他们的语音转文字模型在准确性和质量上领先业界,他们的语音理解模型帮助你超越转写,从语音数据中发现洞察、识别说话者并突出关键信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get started today at assemblyai.com slash sorcery and get $50 of free credits to start building voice AI products.
zh: 你今天就可以前往 assemblyai.com/sorcery 开始使用，并获得 50 美元的免费额度，开始构建语音 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's assemblyai.com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 网址是 assemblyai.com/S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so thinking about the future, what are you most, I don't even know if you could plan out this far, to be honest, but what are you most looking forward to in maybe a time horizon that makes sense for you, but I usually say 12 months?
zh: 好的，那么展望未来，你最……说实话，我都不确定你能不能规划那么远，但你对什么最期待？也许是一个对你来说合理的时间范围，不过我一般说的是 12 个月？

speaker: Unknown
en: 12 months.
zh: 12 个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, one of the things that we will see within the next 12 months is this idea of what we call optical scale up.
zh: 你看，接下来 12 个月内我们会看到的一件事，就是我们所说的光学纵向扩展这个概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what is optical scale up?
zh: 那么什么是光学纵向扩展呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you talked to Tony earlier today, and he's one of the bright minds in the industry.
zh: 我知道你今天早些时候和 Tony 聊过，他是这个行业里最聪明的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're very lucky to get that conversation.
zh: 我们能促成那次对话真是非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: Optical scale-up, if you look at a rack, you look at one of these servers that gets deployed by a hyperscaler and you go creep around the backside, there are a ton of Ethernet cables.
zh: 光学纵向扩展——如果你看一个机架，看一台超大规模云厂商部署的服务器，你绕到背面看看，那里有大量的以太网线缆。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you probably use Ethernet in your house today, maybe to wire your PC as you're doing all your work at home or in the office.
zh: 我是说，你今天在家里可能就在用以太网，也许你在家里或办公室工作的时候用它来连接你的 PC。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an Ethernet cable that plugs into the side of the PC, right?
zh: 有一根以太网线缆插在 PC 的侧面，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at a rack, there's tons and tons of these Ethernet cables, miles and miles of wire that run in the back of the servers.
zh: 而如果你看一个机架，那里有非常多非常多的这种以太网线缆，成英里成英里的线缆在服务器背面穿行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the next 12 months, we'll see some of those copper wires move to optical.
zh: 在接下来的 12 个月里，我们会看到其中一部分铜线迁移到光学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the reality, and Tony and I were talking about it earlier today over at the conference, optics is more expensive.
zh: 现实情况是，今天早些时候我和 Tony 在大会上也聊到过，光学更贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people don't want to do it if they don't have to.
zh: 所以人们如果不是必须就不想用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a more expensive medium than is copper.
zh: 它是比铜更贵的一种介质。

speaker: Unknown
en: Copper is a well-trod path.
zh: 铜是一条被充分走过的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: People understand it.
zh: 人们理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: People understand the expense that there is.
zh: 人们理解其中存在的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And generally, they'll try to avoid using optics.
zh: 总的来说，他们会尽量避免使用光学。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's getting to a point where the physics
zh: 但现在已经到了这样一个地步，物理规律

speaker: Unknown
en: of the back of that rack, that connectivity that sits in the back of the rack is such that you have to do it.
zh: 使得那个机架背面、位于机架背面的那些连接，让你不得不这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we already have a lot of fiber optics in the data center.
zh: 而且我们在数据中心里已经有很多光纤了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have yet.
zh: 我们还没有的，是——

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have deployments in these racks themselves.
zh: 我们还没有在这些机架本身内部部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a lot of connections inside the data center that go out.
zh: 我们在数据中心内部有很多向外延伸的连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call scale out, but we don't yet see scale up.
zh: 我们称之为横向扩展，但我们还没有看到纵向扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in the next 12 months we will.
zh: 我认为在接下来的 12 个月里我们会看到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's going to drive volumes that are unprecedented in the optical industry, right?
zh: 而且这将带来光学行业前所未有的产量规模，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Volumes of tens, hundreds of millions of units, where again, we're sort of used to dealing in scales of thousands.
zh: 几千万、几亿件的产量规模，而我们习惯了处理的是以千为单位的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is the craziest place that this has taken you?
zh: 这件事把你带到的最疯狂的地方是哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good question.
zh: 这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you know, what's interesting, and you probably appreciate this, most of the hyperscalers and the strength right now is in the US, right?
zh: 我是说，你知道，有意思的是，你可能会认同这一点，大多数超大规模云厂商和当前的实力集中在美国，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So US market has been incredibly strong.
zh: 所以美国市场一直非常强劲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our business is very heavily centered on the US.
zh: 我们的业务非常集中在美国。

speaker: Unknown
en: China is a difficult market, right?
zh: 中国是一个困难的市场，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've talked about this, I think, in some of your previous shows.
zh: 我想你在之前的一些节目里谈到过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: The geopolitics of China are very tricky.
zh: 中国的地缘政治非常棘手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Between the US optical component suppliers and how much we supply into the Chinese data centers, very little.
zh: 在美国光学组件供应商和我们对中国的数据中心供应多少之间，非常少。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't supply very much here into the Chinese data centers.
zh: 我们在中国数据中心这里的供应非常少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas Chinese optical component suppliers, some of our competitors, have a pretty big footprint in US data centers.
zh: 而中国的光学组件供应商，我们的一些竞争对手，在美国数据中心有相当大的份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's been a lot of push and pull around the geopolitics of the situation.
zh: 所以围绕这个局面的地缘政治有过很多拉扯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we going to see a world where it gets mandated by either the government or by the customers themselves to use more US content?
zh: 我们会不会看到一个世界，由政府或客户自己强制要求使用更多美国含量的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll see.
zh: 到时候看吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But right now, Chinese suppliers have a pretty big presence in the US market.
zh: 但就目前而言，中国供应商在美国市场有相当大的存在感。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, as we close out, I have one question dedicated to one of our partners.
zh: 那么，在收尾之际，我有一个问题专门留给我们的一个合作伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Rex.
zh: 是 Rex。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're a performance credit card, corporate credit card.
zh: 他们是一张绩效信用卡，企业信用卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're all about spending smarter, moving faster.
zh: 所以他们的一切都是关于更聪明地消费、更快速地行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I take this in a personal lens.
zh: 但我是从个人的角度来看这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm really curious from your standpoint, you've built up a tremendous career.
zh: 所以我真的很好奇，从你的角度来看，你建立了一份非凡的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've been CEO of three public companies.
zh: 你曾担任过三家上市公司的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to think performance, a component of that is who you surround yourself with, who you're mentored by, who you're inspired by, those types of figures along the way.
zh: 我倾向于认为，业绩的一部分取决于你身边围绕的人、指导你的人、激励你的人，以及一路走来那些类似的人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who are those figures for you?
zh: 对你来说，那些人物是谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I've been super lucky.
zh: 瞧，我一直非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you talk about Brex and performance, and I think you've got the right theme and the right partner for what you're doing.
zh: 我是说，你谈到 Brex 和业绩，我认为你们为自己的事业选对了主题、选对了合作伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been very lucky.
zh: 我一直非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: My father, interestingly enough, was an electrical engineer.
zh: 说来有趣，我的父亲是一名电气工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was one of the first electrical engineers that came over from Europe.
zh: 他是最早从欧洲过来的电气工程师之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He actually was based in the United Kingdom and came over just shortly before I was born.
zh: 他实际上常驻英国，在我出生前不久才过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he had tremendous influence.
zh: 他对我影响巨大。

speaker: Unknown
en: He told me as I was growing up, you can have any major you want in college just as long as the last word is engineering, electrical, mechanical, civil, I don't care.
zh: 在我成长过程中，他对我说，大学里你想选什么专业都可以，只要最后一个词是工程就行，电气、机械、土木，我无所谓。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got to be an engineer.
zh: 必须是工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he had tremendous impact, I think, on me.
zh: 我想，他对我产生了巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as I got in my career, I spent a lot of years at a company called Broadcom, which I know you covered pretty extensively.
zh: 然后在我进入职业生涯后，我在一家叫 Broadcom 的公司工作了很多年，我知道你们对它报道得相当多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Broadcom was a very interesting company in that
zh: Broadcom 是一家非常有趣的公司，因为

speaker: Unknown
en: It was bought by Avago and then the name stayed, the Broadcom name was the surviving name.
zh: 它被 Avago 收购了，然后名字保留了下来，Broadcom 这个名字成为了存续的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was a gentleman at Broadcom, a guy called Bob Rango that I worked for for years and years.
zh: 但 Broadcom 有位先生，一个叫 Bob Rango 的人，我为他工作了多年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Bob served on several boards and had a long and prestigious career.
zh: Bob 曾在多家董事会任职，有着漫长而卓越的职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he had a lot of impact on me sort of as a business guy and how I think about business problems.
zh: 他对我作为商业人士以及我思考商业问题的方式产生了很大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's amazing.
zh: 真是了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tony said dead people.
